name: Canvas
summary: How a slide type LOOKS on the canvas — the 16:9 stage, theme/colour/fonts from xprops, semantic state colours, WCAG readability from across the room, framed-vs-full-canvas, presenter controls (host control bar, or in-canvas <aha-button size="xl"> on the Developer Platform), one accent per deck, borders, motion, in-canvas keyboard affordances, and i18n — built from existing components.
highlights: How a slide type looks on the 16:9 canvas
Theme, colour and fonts from xprops; semantic state colours; WCAG readability from across the room
Presenter controls, one accent per deck, borders, motion, keyboard affordances, i18n
lead: The canvas is the visual surface a slide type renders into — one iframe shared by the editor preview and the live presenting/casting screen. It drifts fastest because each slide is its own cross-origin bundle that can't see the host theme. This pattern ships NO new component: it documents the CONVENTIONS that make every slide read on light, dark, and image themes, stay legible from the back of a hall, and reuse the host control bar and the component library rather than hand-rolling. The narrative 'why', the worked BAD/GOOD examples, and the full §1–§9 rationale live in the DS `canvas` guide; this artifact carries only what the repo can enforce.

skillRef.note: This guide is the source of truth for rationale, worked BAD/GOOD examples, the §1–§9 sections, the pre-ship checklist (§8), and the canonical good-fill-in-the-blanks fixture. This pattern distils the enforceable subset; each rule links back by ref to the judge criteria (C1..C16) and/or the skill section it comes from. The judge the DS anti-slop judge (`canvas` surface) emits a binary PASS/FAIL across the same contracts.

surfaceChoice.useFor: a 'question + answer area' slide that should look like every built-in AhaSlides slide; the host renders title/description/question-image and your iframe fills the rest
surfaceChoice.example: a poll answer area, a quiz choice grid

surfaceChoice.useFor: a bespoke layout that owns the whole stage; the host hides its chrome and you render the title (slideProps.title) yourself
surfaceChoice.example: This or That, a custom game board

surfaceChoice.surface: Presenter control bar (NCB, outside the iframe) — built slide plugins
surfaceChoice.useFor: slide-specific actions (Next / Summarise / Previous) on a built slide plugin that declares them in its manifest — painted by the host as <aha-antd-button>, never rendered inside the canvas
surfaceChoice.example: Idea board's Previous / Next: vote / Summarise

surfaceChoice.surface: In-canvas presenter controls — Developer Platform (build-less HTML slide types)
surfaceChoice.useFor: slide-specific actions on a build-less slide type (presenter canvas loads lib/canvas.js, audience.html lib/audience.js, settings.html lib/settings.js): the controls render INSIDE the canvas as <aha-button size="xl">, sized by the attribute and coloured through --aha-color-primary
surfaceChoice.example: Team Retro's Previous / Next stage / Reveal row

composedOf.use: in-canvas presenter controls — <aha-button size="xl"> (52px, read from room distance) on the Developer Platform, or the in-canvas fallback of a built plugin when the plugin-action flag is off; never a raw <button> and never resized through ::part(button)
on-canvas glyphs — the ✓/✗ verdict mark, trophy, status indicators — a design-system glyph, never an inline <svg> or a foreign icon set
a stage / round indicator (Ideas → Group → Vote) — <aha-stepper>, current stage in ink (size="lg" on the canvas), never hand-rolled .step pills and never the primary accent
a type-to-pick field (owner, name, tag) — <aha-autocomplete>, never a hand-rolled <input> + <ul> combobox

result charts on the canvas — <aha-chart palette="deck"> with presentationColorPalette as colors and slide.textColour as ink; never a hand-rolled bar or a chart engine; for a Pick Answer result pass correct plus correct-style="indicator" to keep palette fills (the default fill style follows the mockup's green correct bar)

the deck accent: set it from presentationColorPalette[0] on :root (with the --aha-button-primary-* hover / press / text tokens) so the canvas, the audience view and every <aha-button> show the same colour
the one fixed dark ink (#1A1A1A) wherever the slide needs a dark label — never #1A1A2E (--aha-brand-3 / --aha-indigo-100)
the 1px neutral hairline (#E3E3E3) on a bounded white card; chips 1.5px
hover / selected / expanded transitions, paired with --aha-ease-out or --aha-ease-in-out, on persistent nodes
the ✓ / correct-answer / validation-passed mark — the semantic function token (#16C49A) bundled into the plugin build, never a lookalike brand accent
the ✗ / incorrect-answer / destructive-action mark — the semantic function token (#F5222D), bundled, never hard-coded
the caution / 'are you sure?' indicator mark — bundled semantic function token
the informational badge mark — bundled semantic function token
the radius scale on rectangular content containers — cards and panels 12px (--aha-radius-lg, the DS card), option tiles, inputs and buttons 8px; never above 12px
the host-painted presenter control-bar action button (NCB) — you declare the action data in the manifest, the host renders this wrapper; the iframe cannot call it directly
the in-canvas keyboard-shortcut indicator — a single-character key renders as a SQUARE (equal box, radius 4), multi-char keys grow wider; shared across slides
an icon-only in-canvas button's name + shortcut tooltip (e.g. 'Mute music (M)') — shared tooltip, not a hand-rolled title-only hover
a shared focus-trap wrapper for an in-canvas modal/overlay/popover — moves focus in on open, cycles Tab within, returns focus to the trigger on close

the shared useDeckFont(fontFamily) helper — injects the deck font's @font-face <link> into the iframe so binding fontFamily doesn't fall back to serif; idempotent, no-ops for bundled Plus Jakarta Sans

componentBacklog: composedOf marks 5 artifacts this pattern needs that the DS does not yet ship (aha-antd-button host wrapper, kbd-chip, tooltip, focus-trap, use-deck-font). Per the charter, a pattern that leans on a missing component is a signal to add it HERE — this is the pattern surfacing the component roadmap so the next slide type reuses it instead of hand-rolling.

rules.rule: Design against the 16:9 stage proportions (1280×720 reference), not a monitor's pixels; use responsive layout so nothing overflows or is clipped when scaled large (projector) or small (preview).

Keep a shadowed element's shadow INSIDE the stage padding — the iframe clips box-shadows/glows painted past its box. Size the shadow so its reach (offset + blur − spread) fits the margin, keep it near-symmetric, and don't let a scale-up animation grow the element into the padding the shadow needs.

Read colours and fonts from xprops (slide.baseColour, slide.textColour, slide.backgroundImage, presentation.fontFamily, presentationColorPalette, presentationLighterColorPalette) — never hard-code hex colours, Tailwind colour utilities, or font families. The slide must look right on light, dark, and image backgrounds.

Use the accent palette for chart/accent marks so the slide feels native to the deck — but NEVER pair two palette entries as fill-and-text; the palette has no guaranteed fill/foreground contrast. When text sits on a coloured fill, pick only its label ink by contrast against that fill (readable white or #1A1A1A); never recompute the fill itself.

Loading the font NAME is not enough — inject the deck face into the cross-origin iframe via the shared useDeckFont(fontFamily) helper in EVERY role that renders text (presenter Canvas AND Audience/report iframes are separate documents). Binding fontFamily without loading the face is the serif-fallback bug.

When textColour is unset (the common default deck) and the ink sits on a bounded filled surface whose polarity can vary, derive the fallback from that surface's own background with a luminance flip (readableInkOn(fill)) — never a fixed ?? '#fff' or ?? '#313131' constant that goes invisible on the opposite polarity. Bind every copy of the derived ink to one computed source.

Keep the two colour jobs separate: the chart/visualization layer (bar fills, ring segments, dots) pulls from the accent palette and NEVER carries state meaning; the state-indicator layer (✓/✗, status badge, border accent) is where correctness lives. Don't paint the 'correct' bar green — move the green to a ✓ icon and leave the bar in palette colours.

Semantic state colours (colorSuccess/colorError/colorWarning/colorInfo) must be the design-system FUNCTION tokens bundled into the plugin's own build (imported from the DS package or plugin-local constants matching it) — not host CSS vars (they don't cross the iframe), not xprops, and not a lookalike brand accent that merely reads green/red.

A ✓/✗ glyph is a correct/incorrect signal, never decoration. Use it only where the slide has a real verdict (quiz answer, validation pass/fail); don't drop a ✓ on an opinion poll / This-or-That / word cloud as a 'done' ornament — use a neutral affordance instead.

Avoid the four 'AI-generated' tells: no pastel/tinted wash under same-hue icon+text (monotone, low-contrast); rectangular content containers stay on the DS radius scale — cards and panels 12px (--aha-radius-lg, as the DS card measures), option tiles, inputs and buttons 8px, nothing above 12px (pills/chips/badges/avatars/dots/bar tracks stay fully rounded); display-text weight 400 or 600 only (no 700/800/900); no decorative brand watermark or meaningless chrome — every on-canvas element must carry a real datum.

Attach a per-option metric (vote count, tally, share) to that option's own card — a bounded corner responder-count badge (a darker tint of the option's accent with white ink), not a detached legend or a separate vote-count strip. Don't hand-draw a second redundant rendering (a colour-split progress bar) of a metric the option already states.

Meet WCAG AA as the floor — 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and meaningful shapes — checked against the REAL composited background (baseColour blended with backgroundImage). On a busy photo, protect the text with a scrim BOUNDED to that text (a chip or caption bar behind the line), never a slide-wide panel on a framed slide. Go higher when you can.

A slide-painted surface re-anchors the contrast check against that composited surface — but a translucent tint is NOT a contrast guarantee (only an opaque surface is), and any fixed-colour mark on it (a semantic ✓/✗ token, a palette-accent border) must clear the floor on BOTH a light and a dark deck. A light semantic token on a light surface still fails (colorSuccess #16C49A on white ≈ 2.23:1) — put it on a bounded fill or a dark surface.

Size every meaningful text with a fixed logical px from the Tailwind preset roles (text-base 16 / text-lg 18 / text-2xl 24 / text-5xl 48 / text-7xl 72). Primary content (title/question/answer) sits at body 18px or larger; only secondary meta may touch the 16px floor.

Never a vh/vw font-size on the canvas (vh resolves against the framed iframe viewport ~498px, not the 720 stage, so text-[2.3vh] ≈ 11px), no clamp() px floor (it breaks proportion on the transform-scaled stage), never text-xs/text-sm (12/14px), and no arbitrary text-[…] font-size — pick a role. (em is fine.)

Text is for reading, not decorating — a real word renders as normal running text; never stack its letters vertically, rotate it, or over-track it into a mark (e.g. 'OR' stacked O-over-R in a pill). If a divider must be compact, keep the word horizontal at a smaller in-scale role or let it wrap — never stack or rotate.

Never rely on colour alone — pair colour with a non-colour cue (icon shape, label, or position). Prefer an icon (trophy, ✓/✗) over a spelled-out chip; use words only when no glyph conveys the meaning (e.g. 'Closed', 'Beta'), and almost never stack icon + word together.

Keep chart geometry honest — a decorative indicator (leader chip, trophy) must not change a row's spatial accuracy. Reserve a fixed-width decoration slot on EVERY row (empty when undecorated) or render the decoration as a positioned overlay, so a chip doesn't narrow one row's track and make the chart lie.

Borders are ornament — never derive them directly from textColour and never use a 2px outline at heavy ink. A bounded white card takes a 1px neutral hairline (--aha-border #E3E3E3); a chip takes 1.5px; a deck-owned (transparent) surface takes a 1px theme-aware hairline (color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 10%, transparent)); a dashed empty state is 1px. Fix a marginal contrast check at the bar or a bounded scrim, not with a heavier border. Pick the palette shade (saturated vs lighter) that actually clears the floor on the current composited background.
Don't depend on fast or subtle motion to convey meaning.

Declare the framed-vs-full-canvas choice EXPLICITLY in the plugin manifest (setting.enableFullScreen) — an absent setting reads as 'we forgot', not 'we chose'. Framed for a standard question+answer slide; full-canvas for a bespoke layout.

A FRAMED slide's root element must stay transparent in every display mode and let the deck theme (baseColour/backgroundImage the host composites behind it) show through — it must not render its own title (the host draws it) nor paint a slide-wide background/backdrop/scrim. The only opaque fill it may paint is a surface bounded to its content (a card, chip, caption bar).

In FULL-CANVAS mode you MUST render the presenter's title yourself from slideProps.title (slideProps.value?.title ?? '') — the host hides all its chrome including the title bar, so rendering only per-item prompts/labels silently drops the title the presenter typed.

Never set enableFullScreen: true and enableQuestionTitle: true together — full-canvas hides the host title bar, so an enableQuestionTitle value renders nowhere and vanishes. Pick framed (enableFullScreen off, enableQuestionTitle on) OR full-canvas (enableFullScreen on, render slideProps.title yourself, enableQuestionTitle off).

On a BUILT slide plugin (manifest actions, host control bar available), slide-specific actions (Next / Summarise / Previous) are DECLARED in the plugin manifest and painted by the host in the presenter control bar (NCB) as <aha-antd-button> — never rendered inside the canvas. You don't pick the button component, size, or styling; declare the action data, the host does the rest. This is for consistency (theming, shortcut chips, sound), not audience visibility. A build-less Developer Platform slide type has no manifest actions — see the in-canvas controls rule.

On the Developer Platform (build-less HTML slide types — presenter.html / audience.html / settings.html, each loading its own entry: lib/canvas.js, lib/audience.js, lib/settings.js) presenter controls render INSIDE the canvas: a row of <aha-button size="xl"> (52px, the web-component twin of React <XLButtonScope>) so the room can read them. Size only through the size attribute — never ::part(button) height / padding / font-size overrides or inline sizing; colour only through --aha-color-primary (one primary per row, per-round steppers secondary). The host-control-bar rule applies only to built plugins that declare manifest actions.

A declared action's secondary variant is a SOLID WHITE button (white fill, subtle border, dark label) — the correct resting style for almost every slide action — never a transparent/ghost/outline button. Declare variant: 'secondary' (or omit it, the default); never hand-render a transparent/border-only button inside the canvas.

Reserve the one primary action for a genuinely singular climactic step (reveal final result, finish activity) — or use no primary at all. A repeated per-round advance stepper (This or That's 'Next pair', a per-question 'Next') is secondary, not primary, so the accent keeps signalling the one decisive action.

Pass a reactive boolean to a declared action's disabled / loading — NOT a function. The host coerces with Boolean(action.disabled), and a function literal is always truthy, so disabled: () => votes === 0 makes the button permanently disabled. label is likewise raw text ({{ action.label }}), not a function.

Plugin-declared action buttons are gated behind canUsePluginActionButtons; when the flag is off the host doesn't expose setActionButtons/onActionInvoke, so keep an in-canvas button fallback. Build that fallback from the component library (your own Ant <Button> under ConfigProvider), never a raw <button>/<div>/<input> with hand-written fill/border/radius CSS, and place it bottom-centre where the host bar would be.

An in-canvas modal/overlay/popover traps focus — move keyboard focus to an element inside it on open, keep Tab/Shift+Tab cycling within it, and return focus to the trigger on close. An overlay that opens but leaves focus on the page behind is invisible to keyboard and screen-reader users.

Every actionable in-canvas button carries a keyboard-shortcut indicator, and a single-character key renders as a SQUARE (equal width/height, small rounded corners ~4px) — never a wide pill (a pill reads as a tag/label, a square reads as a key).

A labelled in-canvas button shows its shortcut chip INLINE next to the label, always visible — never hidden in a hover-only title="Press X" tooltip (which makes the presenter hunt for it and hides it from touch).

An icon-only in-canvas button carries a tooltip (and aria-label) that is the button's NAME plus the shortcut in parentheses — e.g. 'Mute music (M)'. A bare icon with no tooltip, or one that drops the name or the (shortcut), leaves the control undiscoverable.

Display in the presentation's language — the plugin runs its own i18n instance and does NOT inherit the host's locale. Initialise locale from xprops.presentation.language (or xprops.currentUser.presenterLanguage) at startup and update on host change; no hard-coded English; use Intl.NumberFormat(locale) for percentages/counts, not .toFixed() with an assumed decimal separator.
Hand the right-panel settings form off to the `settings` guide — the canvas pattern covers only the visual surface, not the settings form.

One accent per deck: map presentationColorPalette[0] onto --aha-color-primary on the iframe's :root (document.documentElement), together with --aha-button-primary-bg-hover / -bg-press (a mix of the accent toward the ink) and --aha-button-primary-text — the --aha-button-* layer resolves at :root, so a value set on a descendant never reaches the buttons. The canvas, the audience view and every button then show the SAME accent; only the label ink is picked by contrast. Never re-derive, darken in steps, or 'toward-ink' the accent per surface, and never reuse a semantic colour (success teal, error red) as a data or series colour.

A FRAMED slide over a photo background (slide.backgroundImage set) keeps the deck showing: no slide-wide scrim, panel or backdrop behind the whole answer area. Only bounded surfaces — cards, chips, a caption bar behind one line of text — may be opaque.

One fixed dark ink on every surface: --aha-text-default #1A1A1A (the canonical body colour). Never #1A1A2E (--aha-brand-3 / --aha-indigo-100) as text ink, and never a second near-black (#000, #111) beside it.

Every interactive state on the canvas (hover, selected, expanded, revealed) animates with --aha-motion-* durations and --aha-ease-* curves on a PERSISTENT node — patch the DOM (toggle a class or attribute, update text) instead of rebuilding with innerHTML on each update, which kills the transition. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

A stage indicator is <aha-stepper> and a type-to-pick field is <aha-autocomplete> (both in lib/canvas.js and lib/audience.js); a sentiment glyph is the matching face (system-smiley / system-sad-face / system-angry-face). Never hand-roll stepper pills or a combobox, and never mark the current stage with the primary accent — the stepper marks it with ink so the accent stays on the one action that advances the flow.

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern — ships no composition wrapper from this repo. A slide type's canvas is a cross-origin iframe app (AhaSlides renders each slide plugin in its own iframe, reading host state via Zoid xprops on window.xprops), so the real composition lives in the slide-type-creator / slide plugin codebase, not here. The canonical correct pattern is the shared fixture anti-slop/evals/canvas/fixtures/good-fill-in-the-blanks/ (the judge's good-control) — diff a new canvas against it. If a shared canvas helper (useDeckFont, a focus-trap, a kbd-chip) graduates into this DS, add a reuse block and it is gated like a composite.

selfCheck.label: looks right on light, dark, and image-background themes; WCAG AA floor against the real composited background
readable from the back of the room — fixed-px type-scale role, no vh/vw/clamp, primary content ≥ 18px
colours/fonts from xprops; semantic state colours from a bundled DS package, not the deck palette; deck font loaded via useDeckFont
enableFullScreen declared explicitly; full-canvas renders slideProps.title; framed root stays transparent

presenter controls: manifest actions on a built plugin (boolean disabled/loading, ≤1 primary, solid white secondaries); on the Developer Platform an in-canvas <aha-button size="xl"> row, no ::part sizing
plugin i18n locale initialised from xprops.presentation.language; right panel handed off to the `settings` guide
one accent (palette[0] → --aha-color-primary on :root), one dark ink #1A1A1A, 1px hairline borders with 12px cards, no slide-wide scrim on a framed photo deck, motion tokens on persistent nodes

whenToRead: ANY presenter canvas of a slide type (the stage the room reads). Holds the one-accent rule (palette[0] → --aha-color-primary on :root), in-canvas presenter controls as <aha-button size="xl"> (never ::part overrides), no slide-wide scrim on a framed photo deck, one dark ink #1A1A1A, 1px hairline borders with 12px card radius, and motion tokens on persistent nodes. Stage indicators are <aha-stepper> and type-to-pick fields <aha-autocomplete>, never hand-rolled.
